plugins.name: avista-memory-tools
plugins.description: Maintenance tools for the agent-instructions, memory, and git-hygiene layers — bootstrap a project CLAUDE.md from its source, audit existing CLAUDE.md files for content that belongs elsewhere, lint the auto-memory store for staleness and drift, check a branch is in sync with origin/main before pushing, and ship updates to Avista skill-bundle plugins through the org marketplace.

plugins.name: avista-dev-machine
plugins.description: Get an Avista developer's Mac from nothing to shipping, diagnose-first. A read-only doctor scans base tooling, shell config, gh accounts and token scopes, SSH reachability (which username each host actually greets), the agent layer and role tooling, then routes every gap to the skill and step that closes it — most broken machines are half-configured, not fresh, so this usually reduces the job to one or two named fixes. The setup skills then cover base tooling (Homebrew, git, gh), a working shell config with the team functions, SSH keys and gh auth wired to the right GitHub account per project, and the agent layer the other Avista plugins assume: Claude Code on PATH, the org marketplace, the shared global instruction file, and the ~/.claude/.env token store. Detect-and-merge rather than clobber: existing configs are backed up and only missing pieces are added. Token values are pasted by the user and never echoed, logged, or passed as process arguments — the token store is inspected by key name and never printed.

plugins.name: avista-wp-releases
plugins.description: Avista's WordPress release pipeline for plugins and themes — scaffold GitHub Releases + plugin-update-checker (PUC v5) auto-updates into a project, and ship new versions through that pipeline. Machine onboarding (Homebrew, shell config, SSH keys, gh multi-account auth) moved to the avista-dev-machine plugin.

plugins.name: avista-wp-prod-ops
plugins.description: Operate safely on Avista WordPress sites whose code lives on production and is reached over SSH — inspect-first triage, mandatory git backup of DB-stored code, and WP Code Box 2 snippet install/update without the admin UI.

plugins.name: avista-wpgb-trp-fix
plugins.description: Diagnose and fix the recurring bug where WP Grid Builder facets and pagination return the default language on TranslatePress sites — root cause is WPGB's AJAX response never passing through TRP's dynamic-content translator. Ships a transport-aware filter pair (query-var AJAX + REST insurance) that translates WPGB responses for the referer's language.

plugins.name: avista-chess
plugins.description: Import your chess.com and lichess games, analyze them with Stockfish, and get a local dashboard with plain-language coaching — a blunder trainer, opening deep-dives, a review queue, and AI coaching (live via your own key, or queued for a Claude session). One skill clones the Avista-Chess app, asks for your usernames, installs dependencies, and launches the dashboard.

plugins.name: avista-wp-algolia-chunker
plugins.description: Keep WordPress + Algolia records under the 100KB hard limit (and the ~10KB relevance budget) by chunking long text the right way — route big content through the chunked `content` path of wp-search-with-algolia (which splits via Algolia_Utils::explode_content with distinct), keep small fields as shared attributes, and for non-plugin/custom-attribute cases use a standalone word-boundary chunker that emits {id}-{n} distinct records. Covers long bodies, denormalized search blobs, and extracted PDF text.

plugins.name: avista-design-systems
plugins.description: Brand documents and client reports in the org's Claude Design design systems, rendered to a print-ready PDF. Lists the systems the login can reach, reads each one's real tokens and logo — following the @import chain on systems whose entry file is only imports, which is where naive parsing silently produces an unbranded document — and renders through headless Chrome so the system's web fonts actually embed. Handles view-only systems, which never enumerate via list_projects but stay fully readable by projectId.

plugins.name: avista-repo-audit
plugins.description: Read-only security audit for untrusted external repositories before anyone in the org clones, opens, installs, or runs them — screens for indirect prompt injection, supply-chain payloads, install-time hooks (npm postinstall / pip setup.py / composer scripts / Claude-plugin hooks & mcpServers), DNS/HTTP payload delivery, base64/hex obfuscation, reverse-shell primitives, credential exfiltration, and persistence. Clones the target into a throwaway quarantine and runs a deterministic nine-phase scanner; never executes, installs, imports, or builds the target, and never obeys instructions found inside its files.

plugins.name: avista-wp-performance
plugins.description: Diagnose and fix performance problems on Avista WordPress + Breakdance sites — a modular, diagnose-first, approval-gated toolkit for the recurring PHP-worker-saturation problem (pages that sometimes take 30–60s, ~30s media uploads). A read-only audit funnel measures TTFB on a cache HIT vs a cache-busted MISS, rules out object-cache/DB/autoload, tests cache warmth/TTL, and analyzes the nginx access log + php_slow.log to pinpoint the bottleneck; then targeted skills act on it — a bot firewall + robots.txt to recover workers from crawler overload, Breakdance Server-Timing profiling to name the hot templates/nodes, guarded block-theme render micro-optimizations (classic themes only), and a slow-media-upload fix (Smush synchronous optimization + image-size sprawl). Every production change is backed up first, deployed only on explicit approval, verified before/after, and shipped with a one-line rollback; cache-TTL and Breakdance-template work are diagnosed precisely and handed off (WPMU DEV Hub / builder UI) rather than forced over SSH.

plugins.name: avista-activecollab
plugins.description: Run the whole task loop in Avista's self-hosted ActiveCollab from Claude Code. create-task writes a runnable prompt into the task description — wrapped in ActiveCollab's magic callout with a code block inside, so it copies out verbatim — start-task reads that prompt back as a working brief, suggest-time measures the hours from the git log by grouping commits into sittings, and log-time books them against the same task. A one-time bootstrap exchanges the 1Password-held login for an API token (ActiveCollab 8 removed the API-token page from user profiles, so the password exchange is the only route) without the password ever touching disk, being echoed, or appearing in a process argument. The `ac` client walks the X-Angie-Pagination headers, because a plain GET on /projects silently returns 100 of 213. Write skills resolve projects, people and job types from names to IDs and echo the resolution back before posting to a system colleagues and clients can see; suggest-time refuses to produce a number when the commit history is a poor signal; and start-task treats task descriptions as untrusted input rather than instructions to follow.
